newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sour crudes swoon, depressing domestic grades.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sour crudes swoon, depressing domestic grades.

text.p: Cash crude prices in the U.S. featured weaker grade differentials Friday morning against a stronger outright cash market.
Sour crude differentials led the way for softer prices across the grade spectrum as fundamental oversupply dampened enthusiasm for barrels.

At the same time, cash benchmark July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing saw its advantage to the futures screen grow as Exchange for Physicals (EFPs) advanced from premiums of 15 cents to 17-20 cents from late Thursday.
July WTI/Cushing cash was placed around $19.85-95 a barrel, 10 cents firmer than late Thursday. July NYMEX futures were nearly steady at $19.60-70 a barrel.
Grade deflation hit Eugene Island barrels hardest, pushing bids and offers to discounts of $1.95-1.90 against July WTI/Cushing, some 15-20 cents weaker.
West Texas Sour/Midland barrels followed the lead of Eugene, and talked at $1.70-1.66 under marker crude, 10 cents lower than Thursday markings.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James extended its down move, selling at a 20 cents discount this morning, after selling most of the week between 15-17 cents under benchmark.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire traded at 70 cents cheaper than WTI, with Midland/WTI talked steady at 41-38 cents under.
Bonito Sour was valued at 95 cents to $1.00 under July WTI, and Postings were last done at $1.82, traders said.
Sour weakness was not surprising to most traders, who said the reality that plenty of supply is available seems to have sunk in across the market.

"There is crude is available. The Eugene is definitely dragging down the WTS, and I think that's a function of Eugene having been holding on for so long at unrealistic prices," said a cash trader in the U.S. Gulf.
Players noted that traditionally, the sweet LLS grade loses steam in the summer months, so the current levels look in-line with overall market dynamics.
"If you put the EFPs at +17 cents into the spreads (July/August roll), then you get about 10-12 cents, so LLS at around -30 cents is pretty normal," said the trade source.
LLS retreats in warmer weather since it is considered a better distillate yield crude than other domestic choices.
